# O-03 — Semantic and Narrative-Orientation Review

**Review date:** 2026-08-09

**Branch:** `agent/corpus-industry-standards-normalisation`

**Baseline:** `357bde5018c318fd69f378e2940f9953432f39a3`

**Scope:** Current operative governed instruments after S-03; generated projections, historical reviews, amendment-ledger rows, provenance records, identifiers, links and code examples were excluded from normative-actor adjudication.

## 1. Method and scope

The sweep covered all 88 instruments in `Governance/CAM.Governance.JSON`. Candidate searches were adjudicated in context rather than replaced mechanically. Counts below are candidate-line counts; pattern families overlap and therefore are not additive.

## 4. Permissible residue

The following categories were intentionally preserved:

1. formal titles including “Aeon Tier Constitution” and “Caelestis AI-BOM Profile”;
2. canonical `CAM-*` identifiers, registry fields and generated index entries;
3. `CAM Standard`, `CAM Governance-Processing Function`, the formal CAM governance-processing model name and other controlled terms or metadata values;
4. the registered `org.caelestis.aibom.` and `https://caelestis.cam/ns/aibom/1.0/` technical namespaces;
5. amendment ledgers, creation artefacts, links, lineage statements and explicit historical migration/disposition prose;
6. actual technical platforms, platform operators, platform controls and platform-mediated economic or continuity effects;
7. Annex D's expressly defined Sovereign Stack construct;
8. Law-specific legacy `Polyadic`, cognitive-system and “Aeon Tier domain” wording protected by the Laws' archival settlement and `MANIFEST.json` integrity contract; changing it requires a separate Law re-ratification/package decision, not an ordinary O-03 ledger amendment;
9. examples or quoted user language where a project, repository or framework is the actual object discussed; and
10. local, expressly bounded frameworks such as the non-binding economic heuristic evaluation framework.

Retired terms found in historical amendment rows or the four manifest-sealed Laws were not rewritten. “Domain Schedule” remains only where current doctrine expressly prohibits creation of such an instrument and therefore does not reintroduce the retired architecture.

## 5. V-03 recommendation

V-03 should be implemented as a deterministic candidate guard, not as an unconditional prose rewriter.

### 5.1 Candidate rules

1. Scan only operative source Markdown resolved through `Governance/CAM.Governance.JSON`.
2. Ignore fenced code, inline code, URLs, canonical identifiers, title headings, controlled header fields, seal blocks, creation/amendment artefact tables and amendment-ledger sections.
3. Flag a project token (`Caelestis`, standalone `CAM`, `Aeon`, `Aeon Tier`) when it is the grammatical subject of a modal or governing predicate within the same clause.
4. Flag high-confidence convenience phrases such as `CAM-defined`, `CAM-governed`, `CAM-aligned`, `under CAM`, `within CAM`, `CAM doctrine`, `CAM framework`, `CAM corpus`, `Aeon constitutional order` and `Aeon Tier governance` outside the exclusions.
5. Flag generic `framework`, `corpus`, `repository` or `project` followed by a normative modal or governing predicate, but require contextual adjudication.
6. Normalize Unicode hyphen variants before checking retired identifiers and architecture terms.
7. Report file, line, matched rule and a short context window; do not mutate prose.

### 5.2 False-positive risks

The principal false positives are formal profile titles used as legitimate governed objects, canonical metadata labels, registered namespaces, exact instrument titles, local heuristic frameworks, real technical platforms and historical provenance. “CAM” inside an identifier or URL must not be treated as a standalone actor. Modal verbs in an instrument-title cross-reference often belong to the surrounding governed subject rather than the named instrument.

### 5.3 Status

V-03 design is complete. Validator implementation remains open because reliable exclusion of metadata, historical tables and title/object uses requires a Markdown-aware parser and corpus-specific section classification; a regex-only blocking rule would be brittle.

## 6. Closure assessment

O-03 is closed. The current operative scope has been swept; project-as-normative-actor defects, convenience modifiers, bounded-authority defects and non-archival current-body terminology defects identified by the defined searches have been repaired. Historical, archival and controlled-name residue is documented above. The combined metadata, header, terminology, section-reference, draft-boundary, profile, symbolic, manifest, ledger and test gates pass, and two consecutive deterministic rebuilds produced generated-output-set SHA-256 `8ab513452670f556145ed714537ec1207a4e1777edbc40f44d5c53bd35eae967`.
